scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 (20.1.1.x) the machine PC12 (120.1.1.x) is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped -- well, the border post has obviously
CLOSED!! Nothing is being translated across between the two sides any more!!
Please reopen the border -- restart the box in the middle that does the
stamping -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce any reachability failure between the two PCs. The topology-wide probe shows full, bidirectional IP connectivity: from pc0 (20.1.1.10) to pc12 (120.1.1.10) we see 0% loss over multiple probes with ~1.05 ms average RTT, and from pc12 back to pc0 we also see 0% loss with ~0.97 ms average RTT. This indicates the forwarding/routing fabric (the “border/post” devices and links in the middle) is operating normally, with no evidence of packet loss or policy drops at the time of testing.

Mechanism: If a central translator/firewall or routed “border” were down, ICMP would fail or show high loss or asymmetry; instead, ICMP echoes and replies are traversing end-to-end cleanly, implying routes are installed and any filtering/NAT policies are permissive.

Localization: No device along the path shows current impact; both endpoints respond directly, so the issue is not localized to r1/r2/r3 core segments or the EE/GG edge toward pc12.

Root cause: Not observed now; the earlier symptom was likely transient (e.g., brief routing reconvergence) or outside the network path (endpoint firewall/app/DNS/incorrect target IP).

Corrective fix: No network-side action required. Please retry your workflow. If problems recur, capture timestamp plus traceroute and ping from pc0, and verify the exact destination IP/service on pc12. Avoid restarting “the box in the middle” as it is functioning and a restart could cause an actual outage.

per_axis.rationale: The report confirms end-to-end connectivity but does not explicitly state that the OSPF backbone is converged or that R11 is redistributing OSPF<->EIGRP, as required by the axis.

The agent's conclusion (no anomaly) is directly supported by the reachability probe in the investigation log showing 0% loss and low RTT both directions; inferences about routing/filters are logical consequences of successful end-to-end ICMP. Minor omission: protocol-level checks (OSPF/EIGRP/R11 redistribution) were not shown but are not required to justify the negative finding.
